To do this rename, the methods with the old names will need to be kept around (but deprecated) for compatibility.

However, I wonder if this rename is necessary? VisionOS is related enough to iOS, that maybe we could just stick with the original names?

@dsnopek Thanks for taking a look! I've heard there's some interest in creating a `tvOS` platform as well. With the changes in this PR, doing that would be relatively easy. With that in mind, I think renaming them to these more general names would make more long term sense. cc @stuartcarnie for comment.

I'm happy to look into re-adding the old names as deprecated. Would you be ok with this approach?

> @rsanchezsaez have a look at [rendering_device.compat.inc](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/rendering_device.compat.inc) and the accompanying changes in [rendering_device.h](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/rendering_device.h) and it's `_bind_methods` function to see how we handle this.

I don't think compat methods are the right tool here, because the name of the method is changing, not its signature. I think this would be about having methods with the old names calling the new methods, wrapping them in `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED`, and then setting `deprecated="..."` in the XML.

> I do wonder if the rename to `_apple_platform_` will confuse people who work on MacOS instead of iOS derived operating systems.

I agree. And naming it after the company (rather than OS or product) may not be future proof if Apple makes another platform that doesn't work like iOS/iPadOS/VisionOS

Thanks again, I'll look at that.

---

I agree with your point regarding naming.

I considered naming the methods `_apple_embedded_platform_` (which typically means, both internally and externally, products that follow the iOS platform model, namely: iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, etc.).

I originally decided against it because `add_apple_embedded_platform_embedded_framework` didn't sound great, but I can see the value of adopting that naming. 

I also respect the desire of not naming these after a company, but I can't think of a more suitable name that is common between these OSes (since these don't apply to Android or other possible mobile OSes). Should I change them to `_apple_embedded_platform_`? Any other naming ideas are welcome!
I have renamed these to `_apple_embedded_platform_`, and added back the iOS methods as deprecated both to the GDScript bindings and to the docs. Let me know what you think.
That's fantastic, thanks @rsanchezsaez!

Thanks! The current code looks much better to me. The CI hasn't managed to get to it yet because of the code style issues, but this _should_ be enough to allow it to pass the GDExtension compatibility tests

`#if defined(METAL_ENABLED) && !defined(VISIONOS_ENABLED)` is scattered all around. Maybe it’s better to define a new macro named `MFX_TEMPORAL_ENABLED`, and replace those conditions with `#ifdef MFX_TEMPORAL_ENABLED`

I recently also tried to compile and export Godot game as native visionOS application. In my prototype I found `windowBounds` has no effect on the actual size of the initial window. But `windowBounds` does affect swapchain. If a value different from the default window size is specified, the rendering content will be cropped to the default window size.

Maybe I made some mistake. But if what I encountered is the expected behavior, we better make the code more clear. We can use the default constructor `[[UIWindow alloc] init]` for visionOS, and leave some comment about the window sizing issue.

If it helps the discussion, the `TARGET_OS_*` conditionals Apple uses internally are documented [here](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/pull/42278#issue-2081533200). It's a very handy map of what nomenclature you can use to refer to different groupings of Apple technologies.

For this case, iOS, tvOS, Mac Catalyst, visionOS and watchOS are all grouped under `TARGET_OS_IPHONE`, which is defined as a "variant of iOS". So unintuitively, "IPHONE" is the term that groups them all.

So there may be a case for naming these along the lines of `add_iphone_framework`!

But if you've reached a solution already, feel free to disregard!
